newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO square off on disputed Jerusalem plan.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO square off on disputed Jerusalem plan.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged on Wednesday to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem in a move quickly slammed by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Netanyahu went to parliament for talks with opposition and government lawmakers on the plan to construct 6,500 Jewish homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa, a hill of pine trees between Jerusalem and Bethlehem captured by Israel in 1967.
"The prime minister told parliament members he intends to build in all parts of Jerusalem including in the Har Homa neighbourhood," Netanyahu's spokesman said in a statement.
Arafat, in the Turkish capital Ankara, was quick to blast Israeli plans to build in the eastern half of the city he wants for the capital of a future Palestinian state.
"The settlement is completely illegal and it is against the U.N. conclusions and the agreements which we signed," Arafat told reporters on his arrival in Ankara for a one-day visit.
"So to continue this policy will push the peace process into the corner and we will face many difficulties. I am completely against it."

Critics said the plan would spark Palestinian rage that could prove more costly than gun battles in which 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died last year after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
Netanyahu has come under growing pressure from right-wing coalition partners and several members of the main opposition Labour party to give the green light for the construction.

"I fear a violent struggle but we must not flinch from it," Moshe Peled of the ultranationalist Tsomet party, part of Netanyahu's government, said while on a high-profile visit to a hill above the Har Homa site with 12 other rightist lawmakers.
"We came here to show the urgent need to build at Har Homa and anywhere in Jerusalem," Peled said.

Netanyahu's spokesman said a decision on a date for building would be made at a ministerial meeting next week. He added that the prime minister had told lawmakers the possibility of building Arab homes in part of Har Homa was "under examination".

The PLO wants Arab East Jerusalem, captured by Israel along with the rest of the West Bank in 1967, to be the capital of a future Palestinian state and has called Israeli housing projects an attempt to cement the Jewish state's hold over all of the city. Israel views all of Jerusalem as its capital.

The status of Jerusalem is to be decided along with other thorny issues -- such as Jewish settlements, Palestinian refugees and shape of Palestinian-Israeli borders -- in "final status" peace talks slated to restart next month.
The United States on Tuesday criticised a decision by an Israeli ministerial committee on Jerusalem to speed up the building of roads in and around East Jerusalem.

"We would have preferred that the action just taken by the Israeli government not have been taken at this time," State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said. Davies declined comment on the Har Homa project.
